full_judgment: 6. As it appears the High Court Division made the Rule absolute holding that the complaint disclosed that the respondent No.1 resigned on 1.4.2003 and the complaint was filed on 7.10.2004 and further although in the complaint there is a reference that G.D. entry was made on 26.7.2003 for return of the car and the papers, but from 19.4.2003 to 7.10.2003, i. e during a period of more than one year and six months, the petitioner or the Hospital authority took no step to get back the original blue book or the original papers save except making a G.D. Entry on 26.7.2003, i. e after three and half months of the date of resignation of the respondent No.1, and further the respondent No.1 returned the car and also the papers as acknowledged by the petitioner by putting his signature on the stamp papers but the petitioner is now alleging that the originals bluebook has not been returned but in the complaint there is no mention when the petitioner found that papers received were not the originals and further, after receiving the car with papers on giving receipt, a great responsibility fell upon the petitioner who can not discharge same by merely making a G.D. Entry after using the car for three months fifteen days and by lodging a complaint after one and half year and moreover there is total silence in the complaint in this regard which leads to the presumption that the original papers might have been given to the petitioner and he might have lost the same during this long period of one year and six months and further since there is alternative process for running the car in absence of original papers the petitioner could take recourse of that process and moreover the respondent No.1 can not be dragged to a prosecution case when it is an admitted fact that the respondent No.1 delivered the car with all the papers to the petitioner long time back and the petitioner acknowledged the same, by giving a receipt on stamp papers. Further, after the respondent No.1 resigned on 1.4.2003, it was the duty of the Hospital authority to collect all the materials from the petitioner before his resignation was accepted. Moreover the gist of the complaint which appears to be for recovery of original papers from the possession of the respondent No.1, does not fall within the mischief of section 409 of the Penal Code and the petitioner could take recourse of only section 98 of the Code of Criminal Procedure by issuing a search warrant and the entire endeavor of the complainant petitioner was to victimize or to harass or to insult the respondent No. 1 before the public in general.
